title: Optimize / Evals — hypothesis triage scratchpad
content:
Meeting purpose: quick sync to triage the recent quality regressions surfaced by the nightly evals run (2026-03-08). Goal is to leave the meeting with a prioritized set of hypotheses, minimum data requests to validate each, and clear owners/due dates for experiments or rollbacks.

Context / one-liner: A/B run (canary vs prod) shows a 4.2% drop in helpfulness on the customer-service prompt set and an uptick in hallucination markers on the knowledge-base prompts after the runtime kernel changes rolled 2026-03-05. Regressions are concentrated at long-context (>1024) shots and when KV-cache hit-rate is high.

Agenda (30 min):
1) Quick readout of metrics (2–3 min) — Maya
2) Walk through top failed examples (5–7 min) — Samira
3) Hypothesis brainstorm + rank (10 min)
4) Action items + data pulls + owners (8–10 min)

Metrics snapshot (from nightly):
- Helpfulness (macro) drop: -4.2% 
- Hallucination rate (precision on citations): +6.8%
- Latency median unchanged; p99 slightly up ~30ms
- Long-context test subset (>1024 tokens): regression concentrated, short-context ok
- KV-cache hit-rate correlation: examples with hit-rate >70% show higher hallucination variance

Top failing examples (quick notes):
- CS-123: gave confident but incorrect policy quote; model paraphrased doc section but invented clause.
- KB-47: introduced wrong product SKU in list (SKU IDs are high-entropy tokens).
- Onboarding flow example: prompt truncation leading to missing context — but truncation logic hasn't changed.

Initial hypotheses (raw, unranked):
A) Kernel change altered the order/precision of key-value cache retrieval, causing stale KV context to be used for long sequences. Explains hit-rate correlation.
B) New attention kernel quantization path has subtle numerical differences at long sequence lengths leading to looser grounding to source text.
C) Prompt-set padding/serialization bug: when prompt + history cross chunk boundary, we may be re-encoding tokens in a slightly different layout (off-by-one) which affects generation.
D) Canary models inadvertently picking a newer tokenizer mapping (rare but possible when model artifacts are swapped in CI).
E) Evaluation harness (postprocessing) changed: regex that extracts citations was loosened, inflating hallucination metric (false positive).
F) A/B routing mismatch: some requests that should have been processed on prod backend landed on canary proxy with older cache priming settings.

Quick risk/likelihood assessment (one-liners):
- A (KV ordering): HIGH impact, MEDIUM likelihood (matches hit-rate pattern).
- B (quantization numerical drift): MED-HIGH impact, MED likelihood (long-context sensitive).
- C (serialization bug): MED impact, LOW-MED likelihood (would produce more deterministic failure samples).
- D (tokenizer drift): LOW impact, LOW likelihood (tokenizer changes are rare but catastrophic if true).
- E (eval harness change): LOW impact, HIGH likelihood (easy false-positive cause and should be checked first).
- F (routing/cfg mismatch): MED impact, MED likelihood (ops config changes last week).

Immediate data pulls (owners + what to return by EOD):
- Maya: re-run nightly eval with older harness regex (restore citation extractor v1) to check E. Deliver: diff of hallucination metric w/ and w/o new regex (due today EOD).
- Luca: dump KV-cache access logs for the failing long-context examples (CS-123, KB-47, sample ids attached in linked_artifacts). Capture timestamps + key ids + retrieval counts (due tomorrow morning).
- Samira: run deterministic local A/B for the three failing examples across kernel versions (pre-2026-03-05 and post) and collect token-level logprob traces (due tomorrow noon).
- Avery: confirm model artifact & tokenizer hashes for canary vs prod; also validate routing table did not group requests incorrectly last weekend (due today).

Short experiments / mitigations (quick wins):
- Roll eval harness extractor back if Maya shows big diff (owner: Maya, TLDR yes/no by EOD).
- Add a temporary canary flag to bypass the new quantization path for requests >1024 tokens (owner: Samira/Luca, quick toggle test by tomorrow).
- Pin tokenizer artifacts explicitly in the canary deployment manifest until hashes verified (owner: Avery, immediate).

Follow-ups & owners (explicit):
- Samira: coordinate token-trace comparison and produce a ~1 page writeup with top candidate cause (due 2026-03-10 12:00).
- Maya: harness diff and recommendation on rollback (due 2026-03-09 17:00).
- Luca: KV access dump + quick analysis (due 2026-03-10 09:30).
- Avery: artifact/hash validation + routing confirm (due 2026-03-09 17:00).
- All: quick sync tomorrow 09:45 to decide rollback vs mitigation.

Notes-to-self / meeting facilitation cues:
- Start meeting by highlighting the customer-visible regressions and why they matter (datasets, examples). Keep technical deep dive to 10min.
- Force a single prioritization metric: reduce hallucination on KB prompts while keeping latency SLA; tie decisions to concrete metric delta thresholds (e.g., <2% help drop acceptable for immediate rollouts).
- If multiple causes look plausible, prefer mitigations that are config toggles or harness fixes before code rollbacks.

Loose ideas (if this becomes persistent):
- Add a fine-grained KV-cache diagnostic mode that records per-key embeddings + retrieval scores for later offline debugging.
- Add an eval path that simulates exact production routing (to avoid partial coverage by nightly runs).
- Create a small prompt-set of canonical long-context failure seeds to run on every kernel/quantization change pre-merge.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to compact decision doc after team confirms hypothesis ranking in the sync.
